geometry.note: 'verified' because representation is 'surveyed' from a rank <=10 source (A15/A25). The six-decimal survey of the MINOS detector paper replaces the five-decimal value of the PRD 76, 052003 paper (47.82027 N, 92.24141 W, 0.3 m apart). It is the midpoint between the two supermodules, referenced to the surface by an inertial survey (University of Calgary, April 1999) with a precision of 0.7 m per coordinate; the paper also gives the Fermilab-to-Soudan vector to better than 1 cm horizontally.
geometry.quote: That midpoint was surveyed and determined to be located at latitude 47.820267 degrees north, longitude 92.241412 degrees west, and ellipsoid height -248.4 m in North American Datum 1983 (NAD 83).

method: Point coordinate taken directly from the MINOS detector paper (arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 6.5): the midpoint between the two far-detector supermodules, surveyed at latitude 47.820267 N, longitude 92.241412 W (NAD 83), 705 m below the surface. Inertial survey precision 0.7 m per coordinate; accuracy_m 3 m rounds that up. The five-decimal value in PRD 76, 052003 agrees to 0.3 m.
name: Soudan Underground Laboratory, Level 27: cavern position (published coordinate; MINOS far detector, CDMS II, SuperCDMS Soudan)
notes: Release geometry (underground): coordinate refined from 5 to 6 decimals and accuracy_m from 100 to 3 m after reading Sec. 6.5 of arXiv:0805.3170; the position is the detector midpoint, not the whole hall.

summary.plain: The surveyed position of the Soudan Underground Laboratory on Level 27 of the Soudan iron mine, 705 m below ground, home to the MINOS far detector and the CDMS II / SuperCDMS Soudan dark-matter experiments.
